# azion_firewall_main_setting (Resource)

## Configuration is the desired state

This resource asserts the **complete** firewall on every apply, using a full
replacement (`PUT`) rather than a partial update. Three things follow, all
intentional:

- A change made outside Terraform — in Azion Console, for example — is **reverted**
  on the next `terraform apply`, and appears in `terraform plan` as a diff. This
  holds for every field you declare.
- Leaving a field out is not "don't care". It means "use the default below", and
  the field is reset to it on every apply. To keep a non-default value, declare
  it explicitly.
- A `modules` block (or one of its module blocks) that is left out is still
  reset to its default on every apply, but a change made to it outside Terraform
  only shows up in `terraform plan` while the block is declared. Declare the
  module blocks you want Terraform to watch.

| Field | Enforced default |
|---|---|
| `active` | `true` |
| `debug` | `false` |
| `modules.functions.enabled` | `true` |
| `modules.network_protection.enabled` | `true` |
| `modules.waf.enabled` | `false` |

`modules.ddos_protection` is always `true`. DDoS protection cannot be disabled and
the Azion API accepts no value for it, so declaring it has no effect — it is kept
declarable only so existing configurations continue to work.

Note that drift is only reverted when an apply runs, and only when state is
refreshed — `terraform plan -refresh=false` will not detect it. Terraform also
cannot remove firewalls created outside Terraform, since those are not in state.

Disabling a module that child resources depend on will make those resources fail:
`modules.functions.enabled` is required by `azion_firewall_functions_instance`, and
`modules.waf.enabled` by WAF rule sets attached through the rules engine.



## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "azion_firewall_main_setting" "example" {
  data {
    name   = "New Firewall in terraform"
    active = true
    debug  = false

    modules {
      functions {
        enabled = true
      }

      network_protection {
        enabled = true
      }

      waf {
        enabled = true
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `data` (Block, Optional) Required. The Firewall settings. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--data))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

<a id="nestedblock--data"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of the firewall rule set.

Optional:

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the firewall rule set is active.
- `debug` (Boolean) Whether debug is enabled for the rule set.
- `modules` (Block, Optional) Modules configuration for the firewall. A module left out is reset to its default on every apply, but its drift is only detected while its block is declared. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--data--modules))

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp of the firewall rule set.
- `id` (Number) ID of the firewall rule set.
- `product_version` (String) Product version of the firewall rule set.
- `state` (String) The state of the current firewall version.
- `version_id` (String) The identifier of the current firewall version.

<a id="nestedblock--data--modules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.modules`

Optional:

- `ddos_protection` (Block, Optional) DDoS protection module configuration. Always enabled; the API accepts no value for it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--data--modules--ddos_protection))
- `functions` (Block, Optional) Functions module configuration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--data--modules--functions))
- `network_protection` (Block, Optional) Network protection module configuration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--data--modules--network_protection))
- `waf` (Block, Optional) WAF module configuration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--data--modules--waf))

<a id="nestedblock--data--modules--ddos_protection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.modules.ddos_protection`

DDoS protection is always enabled and cannot be edited. Declaring this block has
no effect on the API; it remains settable only for backwards compatibility.

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Always `true`. Setting it to `false` has no effect.


<a id="nestedblock--data--modules--functions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.modules.functions`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether functions are enabled.


<a id="nestedblock--data--modules--network_protection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.modules.network_protection`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether network protection is enabled.


<a id="nestedblock--data--modules--waf"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data.modules.waf`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether WAF is enabled.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import azion_firewall_main_setting.example firewall_id
```
